title: Argus Cognitive’s paediatric autism diagnostic secures FDA clearance
key_facts: Argus Cognitive's Neurora received US FDA clearance as a tool to support diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder in children aged 18 months to 12 years.
Clinicians upload video and audio from a standard behavioural assessment to a web portal; the Class II software measures over 100 vocal, facial and gaze biometrics.
It analyses how closely a child's behaviour matches that of children with and without an autism diagnosis.
Results are meant to be read alongside the clinician's other findings, not as a standalone diagnosis.
Latha Valluripalli, Argus co-founder and clinical lead, said 'The clinician still makes the call'.
Development was supported by an NIH small business grant; the article gives no accuracy figures.
quote_evidence: Notably, the results provided by Neurora are intended for interpretation alongside a clinician’s other findings and professional judgment, and not as a standalone diagnostic.
The clinician still makes the call,” Vaulluripalli continued.
why_it_matters_hint: An objective aid for autism assessment, with the clinician keeping the final say.
